## Background

I started this project by analyzing Household Pulse Survey data, with the intent of doing a difference-in-differences analysis; unfortunately, parallel trends were not met, and the sample of LGBTQ+ individuals was small enough that most of the result was just noise.

So, now I'm taking a different tack: looking at states over periods of years, and comparing mental health of the population in those years.

This will require BRFSS data.

# 1. BRFSS

```{r}
#| label: setup

library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(rvest)
library(janitor)
library(haven)

if (dir.exists(here("codebooks"))) {
  message("Codebooks will be saved in ", here("codebooks"))
} else {
  dir.create(here("codebooks"))
  message("Codebooks will be saved in ", here("codebooks"))
}

if (dir.exists(here("data_raw"))) {
  message("Raw datafiles will be saved in ", here("data_raw"))
} else {
  dir.create(here("data_raw"))
  message("Raw datafiles will be saved in ", here("data_raw"))
}

if (dir.exists(here("data_clean"))) {
  message("Cleaned datafiles will be saved in ", here("data_clean"))
} else {
  dir.create(here("data_clean"))
  message("Cleaned datafiles will be saved in ", here("data_clean"))
}
```

```{r}
#| label: fetching htmls

# the BRFSS pages have a common url pattern, which makes this easier
# i'm using data from 2016 to 2023

urls <- tibble(years = c(2016:2023)) |> 
  mutate(urls = paste0("https://www.cdc.gov/brfss/annual_data/annual_", years, ".html"))

htmls <- urls$urls |> 
  set_names() |> 
  map(~read_html(.x))
```

```{r}
#| label: downloading zipfiles

# the data come in ascii format and SAS xpt format; I find the xpt easier to work with, so...

get_xpt_link <- function(html) {
 xpt_link <-  html |> 
    html_elements("a") |> 
    html_attr("href") |> 
    str_subset("XPT.zip")
 return(xpt_link)
}

zipfiles <- map(htmls, ~get_xpt_link(.x)) |> 
  tibble() |> 
  unnest_longer(1) |> 
  rename(urlend = 1) |> 
  mutate(ziplinks = paste0("https://www.cdc.gov", urlend),
         filename = basename(ziplinks))

map2(.x = zipfiles$ziplinks, .y = zipfiles$filename,
     ~curl::curl_download(url = .x, 
                          destfile = here("data_raw", .y), 
                          quiet = FALSE))
```

```{r}
#| label: unzipping data

# first list the contents, make sure there's not multiple files in there
map(here("data_raw", dir(here("data_raw"))),
    ~unzip(.x, list = TRUE))

# now unzip

map(here("data_raw", dir(here("data_raw"))),
    ~unzip(.x, exdir = here("data_raw")))

# now you can get rid of the zipfiles

here("data_raw", dir(here("data_raw"))) |> 
  str_subset(".zip") |> 
  map(~file.remove(.x))

# check it

dir(here("data_raw"))

# a quirk about the BRFSS data is that the XPT files have a space at the end of their filepath; here's a way to remove it

filename_fix <- tibble(old = dir(here("data_raw"))) |> 
  mutate(new = str_squish(old))


map2(.x = filename_fix$old, .y = filename_fix$new,
     ~file.rename(from = paste0(here("data_raw"), "/", .x), 
                  to = paste0(here("data_raw"), "/", .y)))


# check
dir(here("data_raw"))
```

```{r}
#| label: codebooks

# in order to read in only the data we need, we need the codebooks


get_codebook_link <- function(html) {
  codebook <- html |> 
    html_elements("a") |> 
    html_attr("href") |> 
    str_subset("codebook")
  return(codebook)
}

codebooks <- map(htmls, ~get_codebook_link(.x)) |> 
  tibble() |> 
  unnest_longer(1) |> 
  rename(urlend = 1) |> 
  mutate(codelinks = paste0("https://www.cdc.gov", urlend),
         filenames = basename(codelinks))

map2(.x = codebooks$codelinks,
     .y = codebooks$filenames,
     ~curl::curl_download(.x, destfile = here("codebooks", .y),
                          quiet = FALSE))

#2022 & 2023 are zipfiles

map(here("codebooks", 
         str_subset(dir(here("codebooks")), ".zip")),
    ~unzip(.x, exdir = here("codebooks")))
    
# cleaning up

here("codebooks", dir(here("codebooks"))) |> 
  str_subset(".zip") |> 
  map(~file.remove(.x))

codebook_fix <- tibble(old = dir(here("codebooks"))) |> 
  mutate(beginning = str_extract(old, "([0-9]+)"),
         end = str_extract(old, "\\.[A-Za-z]+"),
         new = paste0("codebook", beginning, end))

map2(.x = paste0(here("codebooks"), "/", codebook_fix$old),
.y = paste0(here("codebooks"), "/", codebook_fix$new),
~file.rename(from = .x, to = .y))
```

```{r}
#| label: reading in the data

datalist <- here("data_raw", dir(here("data_raw"))) |> 
  set_names(nm = basename) |> 
  map(~read_xpt(.x,
         col_select = any_of(c("_STATE",
             "_RACE",
             "_RACE1",
             "_AGE80",
             "SEX",
             "SEX1",
             "SXORIENT",
             "SOMALE",
             "SOFEMALE",
             "SEXVAR",
             "TRNSGNDR",
             "EDUCA",
             "MARITAL",
             "GENHLTH",
             "MENTHLTH",
             "PHYSHLTH",
             "POORHLTH",
             "_LLCPWT"))))
```

```{r}
#| label: data cleaning

datalist <- map(datalist, ~zap_label(.x)) # saves a bunch of space

# 2016 and 2017 need to be cleaned separately from the others, bc they have a different number of variables

datalist1 <- datalist |> 
  keep(str_detect(names(datalist), "(2016)|(2017)"))

datalist2 <- datalist |> 
  discard(str_detect(names(datalist), "(2016)|(2017)"))


# first one first

data1 <- map(datalist1, clean_names) |> 
  map2(.y = names(datalist1),
       ~mutate(.x, source = .y)) |> 
  bind_rows() |>
  mutate(across(c(physhlth, menthlth, poorhlth), #mental/physical health days
                ~case_match(.x,
                           88 ~ 0,
                           c(77,99) ~ NA_integer_,
                           .default = .x)),
         genhlth = case_match(genhlth,
                              c(7,9) ~ NA_integer_,
                              c(1:5) ~ 6 - genhlth,
                              .default = genhlth),# reverse coding so higher is better health
         female = case_match(sex,
                             9 ~ NA_integer_,
                             2 ~ 1,
                             1 ~ 0), # making a binary variable for sex
         marital = case_match(marital,
                              c(1,6) ~ "marpar",
                              c(2:4) ~ "divwidsep",
                              5 ~ "nevmar",
                              9 ~ NA_character_,
                              .default = as.character(marital)),
         # collapsing into 3 categories
         educa = case_match(educa,
                            c(1:3) ~ "lths",
                            4 ~ "hsgrad",
                            5 ~ "somcol",
                            6 ~ "colgrad",
                            9 ~ NA_character_,
                            .default = as.character(educa)),
         # collapsing into 4 categories
         sxorient = case_match(sxorient,
                               1 ~ "st",
                               2 ~ "gay",
                               3 ~ "bi",
                               4 ~ "oth",
                               c(7,9) ~ NA_character_,
                             .default = as.character(sxorient)),
         # recoding to character variable
         tgnc = case_match(trnsgndr,
                           c(1:3) ~ 1,
                           4 ~ 0,
                           c(7,9) ~ NA_integer_,
                           .default = trnsgndr),
         # making a binary variable: trans/gender non-conforming or not
         race = case_match(race,
                           1 ~ "nhw",
                           2 ~ "nhb",
                           c(3:7) ~ "othmult",
                           8 ~ "hisp",
                           9 ~ NA_character_),
         # collapsing to 4 categories
         age = age80,
         state_code = state) |>
  select(state_code, source, sxorient, tgnc, 
         marital, female, race, age, educa,
         genhlth, physhlth, menthlth, poorhlth) |> 
# originally 936,319 observations
  drop_na(sxorient)


## second one 

rename_sex <- function(df) {
  sexvar <- colnames(df) |> str_subset("SEX")
  
  df <- df |> 
    rename(sex = all_of(sexvar))
  
  return(df)
} # need to make sure all of these 

data2 <- map(datalist2, rename_sex) |> 
  map(clean_names) |> 
  map2(.y = names(datalist2),
       ~mutate(.x, source = .y)) |> 
  bind_rows() |>
  mutate(across(c(physhlth, menthlth, poorhlth), #mental/physical health days
                ~case_match(.x,
                           88 ~ 0,
                           c(77,99) ~ NA_integer_,
                           .default = .x)),
         genhlth = case_match(genhlth,
                              c(7,9) ~ NA_integer_,
                              c(1:5) ~ 6 - genhlth,
                              .default = genhlth),# reverse coding so higher is better health
         female = case_match(sex,
                             9 ~ NA_integer_,
                             2 ~ 1,
                             1 ~ 0), # making a binary variable for sex
         marital = case_match(marital,
                              c(1,6) ~ "marpar",
                              c(2:4) ~ "divwidsep",
                              5 ~ "nevmar",
                              9 ~ NA_character_,
                              .default = as.character(marital)),
         # collapsing into 3 categories
         educa = case_match(educa,
                            c(1:3) ~ "lths",
                            4 ~ "hsgrad",
                            5 ~ "somcol",
                            6 ~ "colgrad",
                            9 ~ NA_character_,
                            .default = as.character(educa)),
         # collapsing into 4 categories
         sxorient = case_when(sex == 2 ~ sofemale,
                              sex == 1 ~ somale),
         sxorient = case_match(sxorient,
                               1 ~ "gay",
                               2 ~ "st",
                               3 ~ "bi",
                               4 ~ "oth",
                               c(7,9) ~ NA_character_,
                             .default = as.character(sxorient)),
         # recoding to character variable
         tgnc = case_match(trnsgndr,
                           c(1:3) ~ 1,
                           4 ~ 0,
                           c(7,9) ~ NA_integer_,
                           .default = trnsgndr),
         # making a binary variable: trans/gender non-conforming or not
         race = case_match(race,
                           1 ~ "nhw",
                           2 ~ "nhb",
                           c(3:7) ~ "othmult",
                           8 ~ "hisp",
                           9 ~ NA_character_),
         # collapsing to 4 categories
         age = age80,
         state_code = state) |> 
  select(state_code, source, sxorient, tgnc, 
         marital, female, race, age, educa,
         genhlth, physhlth, menthlth, poorhlth) |> 
  # had 2574810 observations
  drop_na(sxorient)


brfss <- bind_rows(data1, data2) |> 
  mutate(year = as.numeric(str_extract(source, "[0-9]+"))) |> 
  relocate(year, .after = "state_code") |> 
  relocate(source, .after = everything())

```

```{r}
save(brfss, file = here("data_clean", "brfss.Rdata"))

```

# 2. Anti-Trans Laws

```{r}
#| label: data acquisition

laws <- list(
  # first two are text-based
laws18 = read_html("https://www.aclu.org/documents/past-legislation-affecting-lgbt-rights-across-country-2018"),

laws19 = read_html("https://www.aclu.org/documents/past-legislation-affecting-lgbt-rights-across-country-2019"),

# then we have a few csvs...
laws20 = read_csv("https://www.aclu.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/legislation-tracker_2020.csv", skip = 1),

laws21 = read_csv("https://www.aclu.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/2021-legislation-tracker_2021.csv"),

laws22 = read_csv("https://www.aclu.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/legislation-tracker_2022.csv"),

laws23 = read_csv("https://wp.api.aclu.org/wp-json/api/legislation/csv/67497", n_max = 510))


```

```{r}
#| label: data cleaning

# need to clean up laws18 and laws19
# this is very ad hoc coding but i really couldn't be bothered to come up with a more general solution - aclu if you're reading this CLEAN UP YOUR ARCHIVED WEB PAGES JESUS H

state_pattern <- "\\b(A[KLZR]|C[AOT]|DE|FL|GA|HI|IA|ID|IL|IN|KS|KY|LA|ME|MD|MA|MI|MN|MS|MO|MT|NE|NV|NH|NJ|NM|NY|NC|ND|OH|OK|OR|PA|RI|SC|SD|TN|TX|UT|VT|VA|WA|WV|WI|WY)"

laws$laws18 <- laws$laws18 |> 
  html_text2() |> 
  read_delim(delim = "\n", skip = 37) |> 
  rename(text = 1) |> 
  mutate(state = str_extract(text, state_pattern),
         bill = str_extract(text, "[A-Z]+ [1-9]+"),
         date = str_extract(text, 
                            "\\d{1,2}/\\d{1,2}/\\d{4}")) |> 
  fill(state, bill, .direction = "down") |> 
  drop_na() |> 
  select(-text) |> 
  mutate(date = mdy(date))


laws$laws19 <- laws$laws19 |> 
  html_text2() |> 
  read_delim(delim = "\n", skip = 45) |> 
  rename(text = 1) |> 
  mutate(text = str_remove_all(text, "(DEAD)|(BILL)")) |> 
  mutate(text = str_split(text, 
            pattern = paste0("(?=(", state_pattern, "))"), 
            simplify = FALSE)) |> 
  unnest_longer(text) |> 
  filter(str_detect(text, ".+")) |> 
  mutate(state = str_extract(text, state_pattern)) |>
  mutate(date_raw = str_extract(text, 
                          "(\\d{1,2}/\\d{1,2}/\\d{4})\\b"),
         date_raw = str_split(date_raw, pattern = "/")) |> 
  unnest_wider(date_raw, names_sep = "_") |> 
  mutate(date_raw_1 = if_else(as.integer(date_raw_1) > 12,
                              str_sub(date_raw_1, start = 2),
                              date_raw_1),
         date = if_else(!is.na(date_raw_1),
                        paste(date_raw_1, date_raw_2,
                              date_raw_3, sep = "/"),
                        NA_character_)) |> 
  select(-starts_with("date_raw")) |> 
  mutate(text = if_else(str_detect(text, ":"),
                        str_remove_all(text, ":.*"),
                        text)) |> 
  filter(!str_detect(text,                   "^(State|Bill|Status|These|Would|doc|Allow|RFRA|d\\.|a\\.|Incomplete)")) |>
  mutate(id = cumsum(!is.na(state))) |> 
  mutate(bill = case_when(is.na(state) & is.na(date) ~
                            str_squish(text),
                          str_detect(text, "[A-Z]+[[:space:]]*[0-9]+") ~
                            str_remove(text, state_pattern)),
         bill = if_else(str_detect(bill, "/"),
                        str_remove(bill, date),
                        bill)) |> 
  select(-text) |> 
  group_by(id) |> 
  fill(state, bill, .direction = "down") |> 
  drop_na() |> 
  mutate(bill = str_squish(bill)) |> 
  unique() |> 
  ungroup() |> 
  select(state, bill, date) |> 
  mutate(date = mdy(date))

######### the other years, thank god, are easier.


laws$laws20 <- laws$laws20 |> 
  clean_names() |> 
  select(state_name = state, bill = bill_name,
         date = status_date) |> 
  left_join(tibble(state_name = state.name, state = state.abb)) |> 
  select(state, bill, date) |> 
  mutate(date = mdy(date))

laws$laws21 <- laws$laws21 |> 
  clean_names() |> 
  select(state_name = state, bill = bill_name,
         date = status_date) |> 
  left_join(tibble(state_name = state.name, state = state.abb)) |> 
  select(state, bill, date) |> 
  mutate(date = mdy(date))

laws$laws22 <- laws$laws22 |> 
  clean_names() |> 
  select(state_name = state, bill = bill_name,
         date = status_date) |> 
  left_join(tibble(state_name = state.name, state = state.abb)) |> 
  select(state, bill, date) |> 
  mutate(date = mdy(date))

laws$laws23 <- laws$laws23 |> 
  clean_names() |> 
  select(state_name = state, bill = bill_name,
         date = status_date) |> 
  left_join(tibble(state_name = state.name, state = state.abb)) |> 
  select(state, bill, date) |> 
  mutate(date = mdy(date))

laws <- laws |> 
  bind_rows()

```
